note: Description taken from Holmgren's 1910 original description of Eutermes coxipoensis (in German), including the soldier and worker; alate unknown; type locality Coxipó (Cuyabá), Mato Grosso, Brazil. Holmgren refers Silvestri's E. arenarius subsp. proximus var. α to this species. The original is in German and the BHL scan OCR is only moderate: decimal points are often misread as commas or colons and some measurement digits are blurred; blurred values are not cited. The species was then placed in Eutermes and is now in Nasutitermes.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier body length only about 4 mm, head capsule dark brown with a paler nasus tip, the head with only a few bristles; antennae long, 13-segmented; worker head length 1.53 mm, head width 1.20 mm, body length 4.5 mm, a rather small species.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule dark brown, nasus tip paler; body rusty yellow to pale rusty brown. Head with only a few bristles; abdominal tergites smooth, with a row of marginal bristles. Head broadly oval, nasus conical; frontal outline with a weak elevation at the base of the nasus. Antennae long, 13-segmented: segment 3 at least twice segment 2, segment 4 distinctly longer than segment 2, segment 5 longer than segment 4. Pronotum deeply saddle-shaped, anterior margin not concave. Measurements: body length about 4 mm (the head length and head width figures are damaged in the OCR and are not cited).

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Vertex plate and transverse band brown, postclypeus paler; head capsule sutures, antennae, genae, mouthparts and the rest of the body white-yellow. Head with microscopic hairs visible only under the microscope; abdominal tergites likewise only microscopically hairy, with a row of marginal bristles. Head broadly oval, the head capsule sutures distinct and of uniform width; postclypeus slightly shorter than half its width. Antennae 14-segmented: segment 3 longer than segment 2, segment 4 shorter than segment 2. Pronotum deeply saddle-shaped, anterior margin very slightly concave. Measurements: body length 4.5 mm; head length 1.53 mm; head width 1.20 mm.
